items.title: Call to Order
Roll Call
Welcome by the School Board President
Changes to the Agenda
Approval of Agenda
Oral Communication
Approval of Consent Items
Adoption of Resolution No. 7, Reduction or Elimination of Certificated Services for Fiscal Year 2023-2024

publicComments.name: Esther Chan
publicComments.summary: Expressed concern about reading specialist cuts and urged the district and board to find creative, sustainable long-term plans to support students.

publicComments.name: Tom Gerke
publicComments.summary: Argued that music programs are scientifically proven to benefit brain development and that Prop 28 funds should not be used as a budget safety net, urging the board not to cut arts education.

publicComments.name: Hannah Ma
publicComments.summary: Asked whether alternatives to staffing cuts were explored, raised concerns about unequal distribution of cuts across schools, and urged creative revenue generation such as facility leasing or technology donations.

publicComments.name: Lauren Abrams
publicComments.summary: Spoke as the mental health counselor at Taft, describing the high trauma levels and barriers to outside services faced by Taft students and urging reconsideration of reducing her position to 0.5 FTE.

publicComments.name: Megan O'Reilly Green
publicComments.summary: Expressed appreciation for the district, shared data comparing Redwood City's low parcel tax to neighboring districts, and encouraged community members to support passing a larger parcel tax.

publicComments.name: Marianne Naka
publicComments.summary: Spoke as the mental health liaison at Henry Ford and urged the board to reconsider cutting mental health liaison positions at Taft, Henry Ford, Orion, and Adelante Selby.

publicComments.name: Lizbeth Estrada
publicComments.summary: Expressed deep appreciation to Dr. Baker for his focus on equity and for prioritizing the schools and students who need the most support, including special education students.

publicComments.name: Saoirse Rafferty
publicComments.summary: A fourth-grade student at Orion expressed love for her school and district, said she believes the community can adapt to budget cuts, and hoped a larger parcel tax could be passed so all kids have what they need.

publicComments.name: Sue Jorgensen
publicComments.summary: Expressed concern about poor communication from the district regarding librarian layoffs, citing unprofessional disclosure of retirees' information and inadequate notice, and said she is not yet convinced to support a parcel tax.

publicComments.name: Ann Barafa
publicComments.summary: A 32-year district veteran advocated for enshrining a 25-to-1 class size ratio for K-2 classrooms in the contract, arguing that larger class sizes cause students, especially ELs and neurodivergent learners, to fall through the cracks.

publicComments.name: Sherry Tsukiyama
publicComments.summary: A first-grade teacher at Roosevelt shared personal classroom experience demonstrating that smaller class sizes (25 or fewer) allow for more individualized instruction and fewer disruptions, and urged the board to permanently cap TK-2 grades at 25 students.

publicComments.name: Jessica McLean
publicComments.summary: An education specialist described alarming projected caseload increases for special education classes and urged the board to open additional extensive support needs classrooms to reduce caseloads and ensure student safety.

publicComments.name: Allison Sudol
publicComments.summary: A first-to-third grade extensive support needs teacher described how increasing class sizes cause unsafe behaviors and dysregulation, and proposed opening one additional ESN and one SLC classroom to bring caseloads to manageable levels.

publicComments.name: Aaron Washburn
publicComments.summary: A music teacher detailed the academic, social-emotional, and cognitive benefits of music education and urged administrators and parents to advocate for a well-funded music program at every school.

publicComments.name: Diane Gutierrez
publicComments.summary: A school counselor at Orion shared a story of supporting a dysregulated student and urged the board to ensure a mental health counselor is present at every school site as an essential safety net for students.

publicComments.name: Lily Milton
publicComments.summary: An Orion and Kennedy parent and Redwood City Foundation board member urged the board to reject the resolution and pursue a more transparent, equitable, and collaborative process before cutting programs, while also supporting a parcel tax and enshrining a 25-to-1 class ratio.

publicComments.name: Dave Privasch
publicComments.summary: Acknowledged the board's difficult position but said it seems unconscionable to cut librarians, mental health staff, and STEM teachers in a high-cost area, and echoed calls for creative solutions before approving cuts.

items.title: Adoption of Resolution No. 8, Reduction of Certain Classified Services for Fiscal Year 2023-2024

publicComments.name: Salvador Gomez Nava
publicComments.summary: Spoke in Spanish (with interpretation) as a Taft parent of a seven-year-old daughter who needs counseling, urging the board to maintain school-based mental health support so children can grow up happy and succeed without the trauma going unaddressed.

publicComments.name: Ana Solorio
publicComments.summary: As CSEA Chapter 5 President, opposed the layoff of any classified employees and requested the board explore cost-cutting alternatives that do not include eliminating classified staff, asking the board not to approve the resolution.

publicComments.name: Connie Hamilton
publicComments.summary: Librarian at Clifford School questioned why three lower-paid LMA librarians are being eliminated while six new higher-paid positions may be hired, argued that her 11 years of experience is sufficient, and expressed devastation at losing her position and relationships with students.

publicComments.name: Beverly Aguilar
publicComments.summary: Librarian at Garfield School, speaking jointly with Connie Hamilton, argued that eliminating their LMA positions is unjust given their combined 30 years of experience, a pending reclassification recommendation, and the difficulty of filling six librarian vacancies, and requested the board not eliminate their positions.

items.title: Adoption of Resolution No. 9, Release and Reassignment of Certificated Administrator(s)
Approval of Release of Temporary Teachers
Approval of Agreement between the Redwood City School District and TeamCivX and Godbe Research to conduct a Parcel Tax Measure Feasibility Study

publicComments.name: Chris Rebel
publicComments.summary: Raised concerns about asking the community to fund both a parcel tax for staff and future bonds for buildings given already heavy tax burdens, and urged the board to be transparent about its prioritization and long-term plans.
